profiles.name: Banking, Financial Services & Insurance
profiles.guidance: RBI's cybersecurity framework and UPI/NPCI infrastructure guidelines call for strong cryptographic controls on payment and settlement systems.
profiles.recommended_baseline: ML-KEM-768 for key exchange, ML-DSA-65 for signatures on customer-facing and settlement systems.

profiles.name: Defense & Government
profiles.regulator: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
profiles.guidance: MeitY guidelines and Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) designation require the highest-assurance cryptographic controls.
profiles.recommended_baseline: ML-KEM-1024 for key exchange, ML-DSA-87 or SLH-DSA for signatures on CII-designated systems.

profiles.name: Telecom
profiles.regulator: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) / Department of Telecommunications (DoT)
profiles.guidance: TRAI/DoT frameworks and 5G core security requirements call for quantum-safe key management ahead of network densification.
profiles.recommended_baseline: ML-KEM-768 for key exchange, ML-DSA-65 for network element authentication.

profiles.name: Healthcare
profiles.guidance: ABDM/ABHA digital health record standards require long-term confidentiality of patient data, which is especially exposed to harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.
profiles.recommended_baseline: ML-KEM-768 for key exchange; prioritise HNDL-critical patient data records for early migration.

default.name: General Enterprise
default.guidance: Follow NIST SP 800-208 and CNSA 2.0 general migration guidance until a sector-specific profile applies.
default.recommended_baseline: ML-KEM-768 for key exchange, ML-DSA-65 for signatures.
